choices.content: The product of the zeros of \(P\)
The product of the non-real zeros of \(P\)
The sum of the coefficients of \(P\)
The sum of the real zeros of \(P\)

question.prompt:
The graph below shows a portion of the curve defined by the quartic polynomial \[P(x) = x^4 + ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d.\] Which of the following is the smallest?

[Figure 1](figures/2000_AMC_12_Q22_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The useful first step is to translate the coefficient and root expressions into quantities that the graph can help us compare.

Let \(r,s\) be the two real zeros, and let \(u,v\) be the non-real zeros, counted with multiplicity. The displayed graph has all three turning points of the quartic, so its outer branches cannot turn again to produce additional real zeros. Only rough bounds are needed. Reading the intercepts and heights from the graph gives
\[
r>1.9,\qquad s>3.5,\qquad 4<P(0)<6,
\]
and also \(P(-1)>3\) and \(P(1)>2\). These bounds do not assume that a plotted intercept is an exact integer.

Because the leading coefficient is 1,
\[
P(x)=(x-r)(x-s)(x-u)(x-v).
\]
Setting \(x=0\) multiplies four negative root terms, so
\[
P(0)=rsuv.
\]
Thus choice B equals \(P(0)>4\). Moreover, \(rs>1.9\cdot3.5=6.65\), so choice C satisfies
\[
0<uv=\frac{P(0)}{rs}<\frac{6}{6.65}<1.
\]
The sum of the coefficients is obtained by substituting \(x=1\), since every power of 1 equals 1. Hence choice D is \(P(1)>2\). Choice A exceeds 3, and choice E is \(r+s>5.4\).

Therefore the product of the non-real zeros is smaller than every other listed quantity. The answer is choice C.
solutions.title: Compare quantities using graph bounds
